paragraphs: R. Chanina ben Torta; see Huna and Yochanan ben Torta above. Jerusalem Peah 3:7:6 [received chapter 3, halakhah 8]: R. Chanina Toratyehu in Chizkiyah's name. Jerusalem Terumot 7:3:6 [received chapter 7, halakhah 7]: in R. Yannai's name. R. Chanina Torta, in R. Hoshaya's name: Jerusalem Terumot 10:6:3 [received chapter 10, halakhah 8]. R. Menashi went to the house of Torta: Avodah Zarah 26a. See R. Elazar ben Torta; perhaps he was his brother. Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 3: R. Chanina Tarti ruled in accordance with that ruling of R. Shimon ben Elazar. A story: a Jew had a cow that plowed all six working days. He lost his property and sold the cow to a Persian. The Persian plowed with it all six days. When the Sabbath came, he wished to plow as usual, but it lay down and refused to plow. He struck it severely, but it did not move. He went to the Jew and said, “Take your cow, which you sold me; it has a defect, for it refuses to plow today.” The Jew understood that it acted thus because of the Sabbath, since it had been accustomed to rest then. He told him, “Come with me, and I will make it stand.” They went to the cow. The Jew took it and spoke into its ear: “My cow, you know that while you were under my authority, you rested on the Sabbath. Now my sins have caused me to sell you to a Persian, and you are under his authority. Please stand and plow.” It immediately stood on its feet and plowed. The Persian told him, “Nevertheless, take your cow and return my money. Every time it lies down, I cannot come to you to make it stand. Furthermore, you will not leave me until you tell me the sorcery you whispered in its ear.” The Jew began to weep and said, “I am not a sorcerer.” The Persian said, “Who will believe you? I struck it with the cattle goad and exhausted myself over it, but it did not stand. You whispered and made it stand; without your sorcery you could not have made it stand.” He swore to him, “I whispered such-and-such in its ear, and that is why it stood.” When the Persian heard this, he considered repentance and said, “Woe to me! This cow, which has neither speech nor understanding, recognized its Creator. Yet I, created in His likeness, blessed be His name, and given knowledge and understanding, do not recognize my Creator.” He immediately went and converted, merited learning much Torah, and his name in Israel was called R. Chanina ben Torta. To this day our sages, of blessed memory, transmit laws in his name. End of quotation, from a small book of tales. The addendum identifies the cow as Vashti reincarnated and the Persian convert as Ahasuerus. See part 1 above, year 3395.
